subject: general
question: The RTI Act applies to which of the followings in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**All Public Authorities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005 applies to **all public authorities** in India, including government bodies, institutions, and organizations funded by the government.
 
• Under the RTI Act, citizens have the right to request information from any public authority, promoting **transparency and accountability** in governance.
 
• Judiciary, legislature, and executive branches of the government are covered under this Act, provided the information does not affect national security or judicial independence.
 
• Private entities are not directly covered under the RTI Act unless they receive substantial funding or support from the government.
 
• The RTI Act specifically excludes intelligence and security organizations listed under the Second Schedule, except when the information pertains to allegations of corruption or human rights violations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Public Authority:**

 
 
• A "public authority" refers to any institution or body established by the Constitution, legislation, or executive orders, and substantially funded by the government.
 
• Examples include ministries, departments, local governing bodies, public sector undertakings (PSUs), and government-funded schools or colleges.
 
 
 
• **Exemptions under RTI Act:**
 
 
• Information affecting national security, sovereignty, and integrity of India is exempt from disclosure under Section 8 of the RTI Act.
 
• Personal information that may invade individual privacy is also exempt unless it serves a larger public interest.
 
 
 
• **RTI Filing Process:**
 
 
• Citizens can file RTI applications online or offline by submitting a request to the Public Information Officer (PIO) of the concerned authority.
 
• A nominal fee is charged for filing an RTI request, with exemptions for individuals below the poverty line.
 
 
 
• **Role of Central and State Information Commissions:**
 
 
• The Central Information Commission (CIC) and State Information Commissions (SICs) are established to ensure the effective implementation of the RTI Act.
 
• They handle appeals and complaints related to RTI requests and ensure compliance by public authorities.
 
 
 
• **Impact of RTI Act:**
 
 
• The RTI Act has enhanced transparency in governance, reduced corruption, and empowered citizens to actively participate in democracy.
 
• It is considered one of the landmark legislations promoting accountability in public administration.
